card.name: Final digit of round lab thresholds
card.fires_on: The final digit (usually 0, sometimes 5) of a multi-digit number that completes a round threshold, such as <100, ≥160, 450 msec or 50 mcg. Mostly in lab-value cutoff tables and dose or QT-interval figures.

modes.label: Lab cutoffs
modes.description: The last digit 0 in a cholesterol, glucose or triglyceride cutoff in a normal-to-high shift table.

modes.label: Dose or QT figures
modes.description: The last digit of a dose amount or QT limit before a unit such as mcg or msec.
modes.example: If QT >45<<0>> msec Sotalol hydrochloride tablets

card.writes: It seems to suppress unit words such as kilograms, inches and miles after the number, so the next word is more likely a lab or drug unit like mg/dL.
card.plain: It fires on the last zero of a round number like 100 or 450 in lab cutoffs and dose figures.
